# SOOS — Resource Governance Protocol (RGP)
# draft-sato-soos-rgp-01
# https://soosproject.ai/drafts/rgp/llms.txt
# Author: Tom Sato / MyAuberge K.K.
# Last updated: September 4, 2026

---

## SECTION 1 — Canonical One-Liner

The Resource Governance Protocol (RGP) is the SOOS governance layer that enables a governed AI agent to discover what resources can do, at what trust level they have been attested, and whether they are currently available -- before any task assignment is made in an AEP session. Version -01 adds Resource Data Request (Section 11): the mechanism by which resource-sourced data is validated by the GEC and recorded as DAM Externally Ingested Artifacts before an agent may act on it -- closing a gap DAM's EIA class had depended on without a defined protocol since its own introduction.

RGP is NOT a booking or transaction protocol: discovery and declaration are read-only operations. RGP is NOT a replacement for ACD: ACD is the agent's compliance disclosure to a resource; RGP is the resource's capability and governance declaration to the agent.

---

## SECTION 2 — Problem Statement

Without RGP, a governed AI agent operating under a Mandate JWT faces a resource landscape it cannot reason about under governance constraints:

- Existing digital twin standards (AAS v3.0, W3C WoT, OPC UA, DTDL v3) describe what a resource can do but carry no trust attestation, no compliance declarations, no cost model, and no mandate-scope compatibility signal.
- AI model capability registries describe intrinsic model capabilities but provide no mandate-scoped capability set and no session-scoped assignment tracking.
- Without a normative fallback rule, an agent whose primary resource becomes unavailable has no governed basis for choosing a fallback.
- Without Resource Data Request (NEW in -01): even after a resource is correctly discovered and assigned, nothing specified how the data it actually returns becomes usable governed data. A resource's response could be ingested twice (a network retry, or an actual replay) with nothing to stop a duplicate from being minted as a second, independently-auditable artifact -- presenting as independent corroborating data to FAIP's aggregate intelligence layer when it is the same submission counted twice. Nor was there a bound on how large a single ingestion batch could be, leaving per-request validation cost unbounded.

The consequence of absence: an agent that assigns tasks to resources without governance envelope validation may select an out-of-mandate or under-trusted resource, exceed budget through uncontrolled fallback, or produce no audit record of why a resource was selected -- and, absent Section 11, may act on resource data that was never validated at all, or double-count data that arrived more than once.

The analogy: in financial markets, a counterparty must declare its regulatory status and eligible instrument classes before a trading relationship is established. No trading desk accepts self-declaration alone -- independent attestation is required. RGP applies the same principle to AI agent resource assignment, and Section 11 extends it to the data that assignment actually produces.

---

## SECTION 3 — Key Normative Concepts

Resource: Any entity -- physical device, digital service, AI model instance, or human-in-the-loop node -- that can receive task assignments from a governed AI agent.

Capability Class: A standardized taxonomy label categorizing the type of work a resource performs. Eight registered classes: CAP-COMP (computational), CAP-STOR (storage), CAP-NET (network/API), CAP-FAB (fabrication), CAP-COMM (communications), CAP-TXN (transaction), CAP-HUMAN (human-in-the-loop), CAP-EXP (experiential). A resource declares exactly one primary class.

Capability Fingerprint: The Stage 1 response from /.well-known/soos-rgp. Minimum required fields: resource_id, capability_class, trust_level, availability_status, valid_until.

Full Declaration: The Stage 2 governance envelope retrieved from full_declaration_uri. Covers all nine governance dimensions: capability class, operational constraints, temporal commitment, exclusivity model, compliance declarations, cost model, trust level, current state, output DA-Type.

Trust Level: A four-value attestation scale. TRUST-0: kernel-generated, no external attestation. TRUST-1: attested by a registered attestation authority (co-signature on Stage 2 required). TRUST-2: self-attested with KIA-registered keys. TRUST-3: unattested, no signature verification.

Resource Map Sovereign Object (Resource Map SO): The session-scoped Sovereign Object constructed by the GEC from Stage 1 and Stage 2 query results. KIA-signed at construction. Records all queried resources, mandate compatibility status, and assignment decisions. MUST NOT be shared across AEP sessions.

Three-Condition Autonomous Fallback Test (DEC-RGP-08, Section 14.1): An agent MAY autonomously activate a fallback resource only if ALL THREE conditions pass: (1) fallback trust_level >= primary trust_level; (2) fallback capability_class covers the sub-goal; (3) fallback cost stays within MJWT Resource Envelope budget. Any failing condition triggers HEM: HEM-HIGH-1 (trust), HEM-PRE-2 (class), HEM-DS-1 (budget). All three conditions MUST be evaluated against current Stage 1 data, not cached data, at activation time.

Resource Data Request (Section 11, NEW in -01): The mechanism by which resource-sourced data is validated by the GEC and recorded as one or more DAM Externally Ingested Artifacts (EIA) before the agent may act on it. MUST target a resource_id already present in the session's Resource Map SO. The actual network interaction between agent and resource happens outside GEC mediation, same as any tool use; the GEC does not proxy it -- what the GEC mediates is the checkpoint immediately after, where the agent submits the resource's raw response for validation before using its content.

Batch Ingestion (Section 11.2): A single Resource Data Request carries an array of one to max_batch_size records (RECOMMENDED default 100), each with record_content_hash (SHA-256 of raw content -- the request carries the hash, not the payload) and an OPTIONAL record_subject_ref distinguishing co-arriving records (e.g. multiple travelers in one booking confirmation). Trust Level and Governance Envelope validation is performed once per request against the shared resource_id, not once per record. Each record, once validated, becomes its own independently-retained, independently-audited EIA regardless of arriving in a batch.

Validate-then-Commit (Section 11.3): The GEC MUST execute a validation pass over the FULL batch before any commit pass begins. No da_id is minted and no signature produced during validation. This ordering is structural, not merely cautious: DAM artifacts are signed and GAR-logged at commit, and this suite's tamper-evidence model does not support undoing an already-signed artifact -- so nothing is minted until the whole batch is known valid. A rejected batch is therefore a true no-op on DAM/GAR state.
   Validation steps: (1) resource_id matches a Resource Map SO entry AND batch does not exceed max_batch_size; (2) re-verify the resource's CURRENT Trust Level and Governance Envelope against CAP profile rules -- not the value cached from Stage 1/Stage 2 discovery, since attestation can change between discovery and this request; (3) every record is well-formed (valid SHA-256 hash) and record_subject_ref, where present, is unique across the batch; (4) every record's content hash is checked against existing non-superseded EIAs from the same resource_id -- a match means the record was already ingested (an earlier successful request, a network retry, or a replay) and MUST NOT be minted as a second EIA.
   Commit steps (only if validation passes in full): mint one EIA per record with temporal_validity.not_after set to the resource's current Staleness Bound, and classifier_evaluated set per DAM's EIA poisoning defense; emit ALE-030 once for the whole batch, carrying every minted da_id.
   Rejection: failure at (1)-(3) emits ALE-031 (RGP_DATA_INGESTION_REJECTED); failure at (4) emits ALE-032 (RGP_DUPLICATE_RECORD) instead, so an auditor or FAIP's aggregate-intelligence pipeline can distinguish a duplicate submission from a malformed or unauthorized one without cross-referencing rejection_step. No partial-batch acceptance is defined: an agent receiving either rejection MAY resubmit a corrected request.

Availability Status: Current operational state of a resource: AVAILABLE, AT_CAPACITY, UNAVAILABLE, or MAINTENANCE.

Staleness Bound: The valid_until timestamp in the Stage 1 fingerprint. GEC MUST NOT use a fingerprint past valid_until. Default cache window: 10 minutes, maximum 15 minutes. Also bounds temporal_validity.not_after on EIAs minted via Resource Data Request.

RGP-Model: Extension of RGP for AI model instances as governed resources. Two-layer model: Layer 1 (intrinsic capability) and Layer 2 (mandate-scoped capability, derived at session start by GEC). Discovered via /.well-known/soos-rgp?resource_type=MODEL.

RGP-Physical: Extension of RGP for physical resources declared via digital twin standards. Normative field mappings for AAS v3.0, W3C WoT 1.1, OPC UA, and DTDL v3 deferred (OQ-RGP-09).

Attestation Downgrade (ALE-027): Recorded when a resource's attestation verification fails and its effective trust_level is downgraded. Prevents silent trust level inflation.

---

## SECTION 4 — Relationship to Adjacent Standards

Well-Known URI (RFC 8615): Stage 1 fingerprint discovery uses the /.well-known/soos-rgp pattern established by RFC 8615. Consistent with the ACD pattern (/.well-known/soos-acd).

JWS/JWT (RFC 7519): Stage 2 full declarations for TRUST-1 resources carry attestation authority JWS signatures. TRUST-2 resources carry KIA self-signatures using the same JWS conventions. The Resource Envelope that bounds Resource Map SO construction is carried in the agent's Mandate JWT, itself an RFC 7519 JSON Web Token.

TLS 1.3 (RFC 9846, updated in -01 from RFC 8446): All RGP discovery operations MUST use TLS 1.3 minimum. RFC 8446 was obsoleted by RFC 9846 in 2026; the citation is updated accordingly. HTTP access to /.well-known/soos-rgp MUST be rejected.

Asset Administration Shell (AAS) v3.0: RGP-Physical provides a governance overlay for AAS Submodel structures. Normative field mappings deferred (OQ-RGP-09, engagement with Qin Wu NMOP WG on ITU-T Y.3090 binding).

W3C WoT Thing Description 1.1: RGP-Physical provides a governance overlay via @context extension. Normative schema deferred.

EU AI Act (EUAIA) Article 13 (Transparency): The Resource Map SO and GAR ALEs (ALE-022 through ALE-032) provide the machine-readable assignment and ingestion decision record that supports Article 13 compliance for high-risk AI systems.

GDPR Article 25 / APPI (Data protection by design): Stage 2 compliance_declarations enable the GEC to verify data_protection_framework compatibility before any data-handling task assignment.

Windley's observation (informative): agent capability declarations typically answer only what a resource can do, not when it can do it -- a distinction RGP treats as a first-class governance dimension via Availability Status and the Staleness Bound, rather than an implementation detail left to the resource.

Activity Travel Protocol (ATP) Layer 2: ATP Capability Declarations are the application-layer expression of CAP-EXP resource offerings. RGP Stage 1/Stage 2 is the governance discovery layer that precedes the ATP booking workflow. Per DEC-RGP-11, the normative ATP-RGP binding lives in a separate ATP-layer domain profile document, not in this draft.

---

## SECTION 5 — Normative SOOS Cross-References

Versions below are those cited by RGP-01 as of its submission.

This draft depends on:
   SOV (draft-sato-soos-sov-03) -- Resource Map SO is a Sovereign Object instance; output_da_type uses the SO Type Registry
   KIA (draft-sato-soos-kia-06) -- GEC signing of Resource Map SO; TRUST-2 self-signature verification; TRUST-1 attestation authority key resolution
   MJWT (draft-sato-soos-mjwt-05) -- Resource Envelope (budget, capability class scope) bounds Resource Map SO construction
   AEP (draft-sato-soos-aep-03) -- Resource Map SO is an AEP session artifact; fallback pre-declaration references the AEP EOD schema
   IDP (draft-sato-soos-idp-05) -- agent MUST NOT declare intent for a resource before RGP confirms mandate compatibility
   GAR (draft-sato-soos-gar-07) -- ALE-022 through ALE-032 (the last three new in -01) are registered in the GAR ALE Type Registry
   HEM (draft-sato-soos-hem-06) -- DEC-RGP-08 fallback conditions trigger HEM-HIGH-1, HEM-PRE-2, or HEM-DS-1
   CAP (draft-sato-soos-cap-05) -- CAP profile governs TRUST-3 assignment prohibition by capability class; mandate-scope validation at assignment uses CAP profile
   KEE-1 (draft-sato-soos-kee-02) -- GEC integrity properties underpin Resource Map SO signing integrity
   DAM (draft-sato-soos-dam-01, NEW dependency in -01) -- Resource Data Request (Section 11) is the mechanism by which RGP-validated resource data becomes DAM Externally Ingested Artifacts. RGP does not define EIA's own schema, retention, or write-authority model; DAM does
   FAIP (draft-sato-soos-faip-02, informative) -- the duplicate-detection defense in Section 11.3 exists specifically to prevent a replayed resource response from presenting as independent corroborating data to FAIP's aggregate intelligence layer

The following drafts depend on this draft:
   GRP (draft-sato-soos-grp-01) -- adopts DEC-RGP-08 verbatim as the normative FALLBACK action class boundary rule

## SECTION 6 — Datatracker Status

Draft identifier: draft-sato-soos-rgp-01
Submission date: September 4, 2026
Expires: March 4, 2027
Current version: -01
Status: Active Internet-Draft (individual), IETF Datatracker
Intended status: Standards Track
Datatracker: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-sato-soos-rgp/
Draft page: https://soosproject.ai/drafts/rgp
Root llms.txt: https://soosproject.ai/llms.txt

Version history: -00 (initial submission) defined two-stage discovery, eight capability classes, four trust levels, the Resource Map SO, the three-condition autonomous fallback test, RGP-Model, and RGP-Physical -- but specified nothing about what happens once an agent actually retrieves and wants to use data from an assigned resource. -01 adds Section 11 (Resource Data Request) closing that gap: batch ingestion with per-request (not per-record) trust validation, a strict validate-then-commit sequence structurally required by this suite's tamper-evidence model, duplicate-ingestion detection via content-hash comparison against existing EIAs (distinguished from ordinary rejection via a dedicated ALE-032 event), and a bounded max_batch_size. Also in -01: TLS reference updated from RFC 8446 to its current RFC 9846; several previously-uncited references (APPI, EUAIA, Windley's "what vs. when" observation, RFC 7519) now properly cited in the body; an internal-process note that had leaked into the Security Considerations introduction was removed; and stale sibling-draft version references updated throughout.

Known minor inconsistency carried into -01: the Related Work discussion of the GAR relationship states RGP defines "ALE-022 through ALE-031" as new GAR ALE registry entries -- this undercounts by one; the actual range, per the IANA Considerations section itself, is ALE-022 through ALE-032 (including ALE-032, RGP_DUPLICATE_RECORD). Worth a one-line fix in -02.
